NECESSITY: If ALLOW(t) then OC(t). Same justification via conjunction elimination.

Any pair {GBP,BD}, {GBP,OC}, {BD,OC} is jointly necessary but not sufficient for ALLOW without the third conjunct.
The conjunction of all three is both necessary and sufficient.

lean_candidate:
-- Lean 4 candidate: abstract logical core only
-- No implementation is verified by this code.

section AllowAdmissibility

variable {T : Type*}

-- Abstract uninterpreted predicates
variable (GBP BD OC : T → Prop)

-- Stipulated definition
def ALLOW (t : T) : Prop := GBP t ∧ BD t ∧ OC t

-- Core biconditional theorem
theorem allow_iff (t : T) :
    ALLOW GBP BD OC t ↔ (GBP t ∧ BD t ∧ OC t) :=
  Iff.rfl

-- Necessity: ALLOW → GBP
theorem allow_implies_gbp (t : T) (h : ALLOW GBP BD OC t) : GBP t :=
  h.1

-- Necessity: ALLOW → BD
theorem allow_implies_bd (t : T) (h : ALLOW GBP BD OC t) : BD t :=
  h.2.1

-- Necessity: ALLOW → OC
theorem allow_implies_oc (t : T) (h : ALLOW GBP BD OC t) : OC t :=
  h.2.2

-- Sufficiency: GBP ∧ BD ∧ OC → ALLOW
theorem gbp_bd_oc_implies_allow (t : T)
    (hg : GBP t) (hb : BD t) (ho : OC t) :
    ALLOW GBP BD OC t :=
  ⟨hg, hb, ho⟩

-- Individual necessity, not sufficiency (demonstrated by lack of proof without all three)
-- (No theorem claimed that GBP alone suffices — such a theorem would be unprovable.)

end AllowAdmissibility
